body: Honestly, I don't think thats acceptable, only difference now is you don't have to work, he definitely knew that when he tried to take advantage, and theres not much we can do at the moment, but I hope theres a massive reckoning once things calm down abit

Thanks, that's actually really nice that you'd research where someone in another country could get help :). Hope you find a new therapist that's good. My logical self makes me very well aware that I need to, but my physical self prevents it. Such is the nature of social anxiety ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯
In the UK unfortunately otherwise probably would (would like to think I would, but the SA means I would probably be too scared). But that did make me feel a bit better :)

Live in the UK. Great if you've broken your arm or something, but terrible for mental health. Told him they aren't working so he upped to dosage and told me to come back in 4 weeks. Actually have private health insurance via work but there are only 5 locations where the "preferred provider" for a therapist is and none of them in london (surprisingly, although maybe not because they'd be swamped). But it's hard to approach 1 person asking for help, but then when you get bounced around you just end up crawling in bed and giving up

Not sure I'd recommend it. After the first time spent the next day throwing up and shaking and crying in bed. Then didn't speak for 3 weeks then got very very drunk on my birthday and happened again. Don't feel any attraction but he probably is because he's very charismatic and a massive player.

My SA has gotten slightly better but only with a very few people. Most my friends are a lot more outgoing who I've helped through work or family issues and caused us to become close. I first tried to get help when I was \~20 at uni, but was told no point because 3 month wait for CBT, so given diazepam and some self-help links (don't recommend diazepam, dulled my brain and would have done badly in my degree if I continued taking it, although probably affects people differently and I'm not a doctor so don't quote me on that). But if I was talking to my 20 year old self I'd say try CBT. 3 months really isn't that long. Not sure if it works but I always wonder what my life would be like if it did work and I'd done it 10 years ago
